agent: selection wave, reader B (several on screen: the multi-unit panel)
question: When multi_unitpanel shows, its desc, the list of rows - built, ordered, laid out, scrolled, refreshed - a click on a row, and every button and checkbox of the panel: when shown and enabled, tooltip, what it posts and for which units.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::AddUnitRow
addresses.comment: **Slot 34: a selected unit gets a row.** Called by CUnit::OnSelected (0x5C08A5) unless the global byte 0x1A855F6 is set (no writer in .text). In order: CloseOrdersView; the chat list (+0x1354) is moved to x 350 keeping its home y (+0x1D52); a CUnitView(unit, this, inPanel 0, the kept-rows list +0x1DE4) is made - the `unitpanel` window, the single panel's header row - and appended to the row list (+0xD20 first, +0xD24 last, +0xD28 count; 0x10-byte nodes {row, prev, next, byte}), so **rows are in the order the units were selected**; unless a box drag is in progress (0x64D850) CInGameIdler_LayoutUnitPanels. With the count now 2: multi_unitpanel shown, the upgrades window closed (0x66B7B0), multiunit_slider (+0x136C) hidden, the window at +0x1360 put away (0x7395E0). With the count 1: the single panel (+0x135C) is given the unit and rebuilt (0x762F40) and placed beside the side menu and the +0x1360 window. Then the reorganise window is closed if up, and `desc` is set to the count, a space, and ARMIES / NAVIES / AIRWINGS by the FIRST row's unit (slot 15 land, else slot 16 naval, else air) - '3 Land Units'. With the count 1 every row's window is hidden. No test that the unit already has a row. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6639E0..0x664154 (`ret 4`): `push 0x188; call new` then 0x769940 with (unit, ebx, 0, [ebx+0x1DE4]) at 0x663A53..0x663A61; node append at 0x663A7B..0x663AC1; `cmp eax,2` 0x663ADF and `cmp eax,1` 0x663B19; 'ARMIES'/'NAVIES'/'AIRWINGS' (0x15CE528/30/38) and 'desc' (0x15CE544) through slots 15/16 of the first row's +0x28. Only holder: CInGameIdler slot 34 (vtable.py --holding). Caller CUnit::OnSelected at 0x5C08A5 (`call [edx+0x88]`). Wrong if another caller adds rows for a non-unit.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::RemoveUnitRow
addresses.comment: **Slot 35: a deselected unit loses its row.** Called by CUnit::OnDeselected (0x5C0BC1, same 0x1A855F6 gate). CloseOrdersView; every row whose unit (+0x28) is this one is unlinked and freed (count down), or, while +0xD2C is set, only marked in its node's byte; the row is destroyed (slot 0). Then, unless the whole selection is being cleared (+0x1CC8), CInGameIdler_LayoutUnitPanels. Fewer than 2 rows: multi_unitpanel hidden and the upgrades window closed. Exactly 1: the single panel takes the remaining row's unit and is rebuilt, the +0x1360 window put away, every row's window hidden. 0 or 2+: the single panel is hidden (CSingleUnitPanel_Hide) and ShowSelection(null) (slot 32) clears the map markers. Then the reorganise window closed if up; with rows left, `desc` rebuilt as in AddUnitRow; with none, the chat list goes back to its home position (+0x1D50). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x664210..0x664A59: the match `cmp [edi+0x28],eax` 0x664258, the guard `cmp byte [ebx+0xd2c],0` 0x664278, `dec [ebx+0xd28]` 0x6642C0, `cmp byte [ebx+0x1cc8],0` 0x6642D8, the count tests at 0x6642E8/0x664309, 0x763050 at 0x664363 and `call [edx+0x80]` with 0 at 0x664374, +0x1D50 read at 0x6648BD. Only holder: slot 35. Caller CUnit::OnDeselected 0x5C0BC1.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::DeselectLater
addresses.comment: **Slot 43: queue a deselection for the end of this frame's panel pass.** Appends the selectable to the vector at +0xA90 (end +0xA94); with a null, appends every thing now selected. CInGameIdler_UpdatePanels, at its end, deselects (slot 45) each queued thing that is still in the selection and empties the vector. Used by a row's remove and select-only buttons, which run while the rows are on screen. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B.2.
addresses.evidence: 0x656BB0..0x656C36: `cmp [ebp+8],0` then `lea edi,[ecx+0xa90]; call 0x86CC20` (push_back), the null arm walking +0x1304; the drain at 0x651623..0x651680 in UpdatePanels calls `[edx+0xb4]` (slot 45) for each element found in the selection. Only holder slot 43. This corrects FINDINGS-unitpanel.md section 4, which read a null as 'clear the selection' at once.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Deselect
addresses.comment: **Slot 45: take one thing out of the selection now.** Unlinks its node from +0x1304, clears its selected byte (+4), calls its OnDeselected (slot 5) - for a unit, RemoveUnitRow - and sets selection_changed (+0x1D3C) where it is an air unit (kind 2). With a null, does the same for every selected thing. CGameState::RemoveUnit calls it for a dying unit that is selected and, for a fleet, for each selected unit it carries (0x684FB8, 0x684FD6). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, sections B.2 and B.7.
addresses.evidence: 0x656C40..0x656CCA: list walk for the node, `call 0x5D49D0` (CList remove), `mov byte [edi+4],0`, `call [eax+0x14]`, `call [edx+4]; cmp eax,2; mov byte [ebx+0x1d3c],1`. Only holder slot 45. RemoveUnit's two calls `call [edx+0xb4]` at 0x684FBE and 0x684FDD, each after `cmp byte [x+4],0`.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_LayoutUnitPanels
addresses.comment: Places the single unit panel: its x is the open side menu's width (0x6652D0 says one is open; its window's slot 24) plus, where the +0x1360 window is up (+0xF4), the widths of its two parts; its y kept. Then with exactly one row that row's window is hidden, otherwise CInGameIdler_LayoutUnitRows(null). Called by AddUnitRow and RemoveUnitRow. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x663400..0x6634E5 (bare ret, the idler in EAX as both callers set it: 0x663AD2 `mov eax,ebx`, 0x6642E1). 'Width' for the side menu's slot 24 rests on 0x6634F0 using slot 24 (+0x60) as the extent added to slot 26 (+0x68) the position - inferred, a screenshot with a side menu open would settle it.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_LayoutUnitRows
addresses.comment: **Lays out the rows of several selected units.** x0 = the side menu's width and the +0x1360 window's parts as in LayoutUnitPanels. Where there are more rows (+0xD28) than fit (unitlist_rows, +0x1DF8 = (screen height - unitlist_start.y) / unitlist_offset.y - 1): x0 += unitlist_offset.x (16); multiunit_slider is sized to unitlist_offset.y * rows-that-fit high (0xA9EDB0, width -1), placed at (unitlist_start.x, unitlist_start.y - the panel's y) inside the panel, shown, and first = trunc((rows - fit) * value / (max / 1000)) in single precision; otherwise the slider is hidden and first = 0. Then with two rows or more, row i in list order is hidden where i < first or i >= first + fit, else placed at (unitlist_start.x + x0, unitlist_start.y + k * unitlist_offset.y) for the k-th row shown, shown, and updated (its slot 8, CUnitView::Update). With outUnits, every row's unit is appended to it, shown or not. Called every frame by CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView while no country view is open, and by LayoutUnitPanels. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6636A0..0x6639D0 (`ret 4`, idler in EAX): `cmp ecx,[esi+0x1df8]` 0x66372D, `movsx edx, word [esi+0x1df4]; add ebx,edx`, `imul cx,[esi+0x1df8]` with 0xFFFF, call 0xA9EDB0, +0x1DF0/+0x1DF2 into the slider's +0x74/+0x78, `fild [+0x230]; fdiv 1000.0`, (count - fit) * ratio, `cvttss2si`; the row loop from 0x6638D8 with +0x1DF6 added per shown row. The (0,144) and (16,40) figures are FINDINGS-gui.md's.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_ScrollUnitRows
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CInGameIdler_ScrollUnitRows(CInGameIdler* idler@ESI, void* event@stack:4, int* point@stack:8) @AL
addresses.comment: **The mouse wheel over the rows.** Only while multiunit_slider is shown (+0x43) and for an event of kind 4 (+0x14, the wheel by its use): where the point lies within the panel's x extent and between the panel's top and its bottom plus unitlist_offset.y * rows-that-fit, the slider's value becomes value - wheel * (max / 1000) / (rows - fit), the wheel figure from the input object's slot 21 (+0x54), held to [min/1000, max/1000] and set (0xAA0000); the event is marked handled (+0x18) and true answered. One unit of the wheel figure is one row. Called from the screen's event loop at 0x651BE4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6634F0..0x66369C (`ret 8`): `cmp byte [eax+0x43],0`, `cmp dword [ecx+0x14],4`, the panel's slot 26 (+0x68) and slot 24 (+0x60) bounds, `imul ecx,[esi+0x1df8]`, `call [edx+0x54]` on [esi+0x64] then `neg eax`, +0x22C and +0x230 divided by 1000.0, `comisd` clamps, `call 0xaa0000`, `mov byte [edx+0x18],1`. addresses.name: CInGameIdler_UpdatePanels
addresses.revises: Read whole for the multi-unit panel: the waiting selection is the rows kept by Shift on a row's select-only button and is applied only once Shift is up; the 'kind of the first one' is the first kept row's; the per-frame rules of highercomm, detach, the three checkboxes, disband, upgrade_all and reorganizebutton, and the deferred deselections at the end, are added. Confidence raised.
addresses.comment:
**The in-game screen's per-frame work on its panels**, called once from CInGameIdler::Update (0x655E2E); 0x650700 to the `ret 4` at 0x651695. In order:

1. **The kept rows (+0x1DE4).** Where the list holds rows and its byte +0x10 is set, and **input slot 10 (Shift) is not held**: the rows' units are collected, the selection cleared, and each unit not yet selected whose slot 2 allows it is selected (CSelectable_Select) where the selection is empty or its kind (slot 1) is that of the first now selected - so the first kept row decides the kind; the byte cleared and the list freed. The rows are put there by CUnitView::OnSelectOnlyThis with Shift.
2. The reorganise window (+0x1358), where up and 0x7646D0 says no, is closed (slot 50).
3. One row and no battle view: CSingleUnitPanel_RefreshIfChanged (+0x135C). The battle view updated or dropped. ProvinceView_Update where the province view is shown.
4. **Two rows or more** (+0xD28): the three carrying buttons (FINDINGS-transport.md C.3); `highercomm_multiunit` enabled where CInGameIdler_CollectForHigherCommand answers non-zero, the custom-game lock (0x4208B0) is off, and, in a custom game, 0x420EB0 allows it; `detach_multiunit` enabled where CInGameIdler_CollectDetachable answers non-zero and the lock is off; the three checkboxes, `disband_multiunit` and `upgrade_all` enabled (checkbox byte +0x136 = 1, refreshed through 0xA81AA0) unless the lock is on, when they are disabled and upgrades_window closed; then **each checkbox ticked (+0x60 and +0x100 = 1) where at least one selected unit has its flag** (CountSelectedUnitFlags: upgrade_prio, reinforcements_active, upgrade_active) and otherwise cleared - unless its byte +0xD8 is set while it is disabled. There is no third state for units that disagree.
5. Every frame, whatever the count: `reorganizebutton` enabled where exactly two things are selected (slot 51), disabled otherwise - CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView, later in the same frame, sets it again by its own rule while no country view is open.
6. **The deferred deselections**: each thing queued at +0xA90 by DeselectLater (slot 43) that is still selected is deselected (slot 45), and the queue emptied.

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section B, and FINDINGS-transport.md, section C.3.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x650700..0x651695 read whole: +0x1DE4 tests 0x65071F..0x650735, input slot 10 `call [eax+0x28]` on state+0xBE8 ->+0x1C at 0x6507B1..0x6507C3, Selection_Clear 0x65085F, the slot-2 and kind tests 0x650889..0x6508C0, CSelectable_Select 0x6508CB; 0x41C4E0/0x420EB0 at 0x650E0A..0x650E21; 0x669EB0 0x650E6F; 0x669DE0 0x650F2A; the +0x136 writes and 0xA81AA0 calls 0x650FCF..0x6510A0 and 0x651288..0x65133E; 0x669D50 0x651181; +0x60/+0x100 writes 0x6511C5, 0x65145E, 0x6514AF; slot 51 `call [edx+0xcc]` 0x65158B; the +0xA90 drain 0x651623..0x651680 with `call [edx+0xb4]`. +0x136 is the checkbox's enabled byte by 0xA81AA0 (it draws a disabled frame without it); +0xD8 and +0x100 not identified.

struct_fields.name: upgrade_targets
struct_fields.revises: Was `unused_list` (CList), 'not seen in use'. It is read as the begin of an array of 16-byte entries indexed by a definition's type index, each holding a vector of type indexes (begin +0, end +4) - the types that type upgrades to.
struct_fields.comment: Begin of an array, one 16-byte entry per sub-unit type in type-index order (a definition's +0x24), each entry's first two words the begin and end of a vector of the type indexes that type may be upgraded to - by its use, common/unit_upgrades.txt, whose own comment says the rule is transitive. Read by the multi-unit panel's upgrade_all count and click.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x66B17F..0x66B194: `mov ebx,[edx+0x24]; shl ebx,4; add ebx,[eax+0xb0]; mov eax,[ebx+4]; sub eax,[ebx]; sar eax,2`, then `[ebx]` indexed for each int; the same shape in 0x66B2A0. The tie to unit_upgrades.txt is inferred: FINDINGS-startup.md has that file loaded into CSubUnitDataBase, and its writer here was not read. Wrong if +0xB0 is a CList whose first node happens to sit before such an array - the arithmetic indexes it directly, which a list head cannot support.
